S32 E15 — Auburndale: Systems, Security and Surfaces Take Shape
Wood island top with a distressed finish; installing his and hers closets; installing a wireless security system; high-efficiency two-stage air conditioning system; hot water system; installing a marble kitchen window stool and granite countertops.

title: This Old House
description:
S32 E16 — Auburndale: Transformation Complete!
Finishing exterior low-voltage lighting; new composite shutters that add character; showing the hops vines planted to grow on the pergola; water-saving plumbing fixtures; the interior lighting plan, kitchen, master bedroom and bathroom are revealed.

title: This Old House
description:
S32 E17 — Los Angeles: TOH Goes Hollywood, Almost
Expanding and renovating a 1933 Spanish colonial revival project house in the hillside neighborhood of Silver Lake while keeping its character; a major kitchen renovation; a second floor addition; reconfiguration of the back half of the first floor.

title: This Old House
description:
S32 E18 — Los Angeles: Only in LA
A stop at a major Los Angeles movie studio; the back of a house has been demolished: no walls or roof remain; a facility where earthquakes are replicated to help develop ways to protect buildings from damage; heating and cooling systems.

title: This Old House
description:

Kevin arrives at the L.A. house to find the clay roof tiles on site as well as the custom windows and doors; strict California energy codes; the plan for the new roof; polypropylene underlayment; flashing details; stucco.

title: This Old House
description:
S32 E20 — Los Angeles: Secrets of Silver Lake
Norm wrestles with replicating the arch details from the living room in various openings in the house; the stucco system starts on the new addition with the scratch coat; Norm shows the formaldehyde-free batt insulation used in the basement.

title: This Old House
description:

Alfonso uses custom foam forms to create a tray ceiling; Norm visits cabinetmaker Larry Bucklan; Kevin finds a stain on dining room ceiling and a large hole in front entry; Angel Leon explains that the main house roof will have to be replaced.

title: This Old House
description:
S32 E22 — Los Angeles: Spanish Style: Stucco, Ornamental Iron, Hand Glazed Tile
The last steps of the stucco system, embedded mesh for strength and crack protection and a top layer with integrated color and a sand texture; new period-appropriate ornamental ironwork; how the reproduction tile for the project is being hand glazed.

title: Ask This Old House
description:

Richard helps a homeowner replace a shower valve that mysteriously shuts off; Tom shows how to patch a hole in baseboard; Roger shares some tips for maintaining a lawn mower.

title: Ask This Old House
description:
S12 E22 — Special 300th Episode
In this special program, the guys celebrate 300 episodes of "Ask This Old House" by looking back at some of their best moments and revealing some behind-the-scenes secrets.

title: Ask This Old House
description:
S12 E23 — Table; Stumps; Solar
Tom and Kevin build a simple table from solid fir normally used for building decks, and Kevin works with a wood finishing expert to stain and finish it; how to get rid of tree stumps using a gas-powered stump grinder; the state of solar energy.

title: Ask This Old House
description:
S12 E24 — Accessibility Projects
Kevin helps make a home accessible for a homeowner in a wheelchair by modifying a bathroom and several different sets of stairs; Tom and Kevin rebuild a dangerous staircase for a survivor of the Boston Marathon bombing.

title: Ask This Old House
description:

Electrician Scott Caron replaces outdated fluorescent under-cabinet lights with new LED fixtures; Roger and Kevin demonstrate how to work with concrete; Richard teaches Tom about the potential energy savings of temperature setbacks on thermostats.

title: Ask This Old House
description:

Tom and Kevin help a homeowner install new cabinets; Richard shows many options for countertops, including laminate, wood, engineered stone, and natural stone; the Cleveland home and restaurant kitchens of chef Michael Symon provide inspiration.

title: Ask This Old House
description:

title: Ask This Old House
description:

Roger heads to Florida to learn about citrus greening, a disease that's killing citrus trees across the state; the guys ask What Is It?; Tom replaces an old vinyl peel-and-stick floor with ceramic tile.

title: Ask This Old House
description:

title: Ask This Old House
description:

title: Ask This Old House
description:

Roger learns from a beekeeper how to set up a beehive for a homeowner; Scott Caron adds lighting to a dark kitchen without having to run any new wiring.

Helping a homeowner lay sod in his backyard; What Is It?; Tom shares a tip about finding measurements without doing math; installing a wireless thermostat to control a heating system; an app that allows the thermostat to be controlled remotely.

Landscape contractor Roger Cook works with a fencing contractor to install a vinyl privacy fence; Richard replaces a clogged shower valve.

Landscape contractor Roger Cook shows a homeowner how to properly apply bulk pine bark mulch to his garden beds; Richard installs a natural gas line for a barbecue grill.

Work on the L.A. project wraps up with finishing touches; the new HVAC system, bathrooms, plaster detail, landscaping and irrigation system; a mix of antiques, reproductions and upholstery create inviting spaces; the master suite and the new kitchen.

This Old House opens a new season with a 300-year-old Colonial farmstead; the homeowners plan to preserve the historic part of the house, while adding space and modern amenities with two small additions; Tom inspects the structure.

Transplanting shrubs and plants out front; a 3-D architectural model; removing the front entry porch, accessibility ramp and rotted clapboards; layout for the new addition; a drain and sump pump system; Mark demos the exterior parts of the chimney.

Norm continues removing the old clapboards; Tom and Mark carefully open up a hole in the old fieldstone foundation that will connect the old basement space to the new; Alison Hardy removes historic sashes to be taken off site for rehab.

Framing up the walls of the entry addition; creating the connection to the main house; repairing the chimney; removing the fireplace from the kitchen; revisiting the Acton Project; recent discoveries from the job site.

title: This Old House
description:

Landscape designer Jenn Nawada shows the site plan; removing invasive vines and brambles from the backyard; raising a new family room gable wall; repairing a historic window sill; demolishing the ceiling to regain head height for the kitchen.

title: This Old House
description:

The benefits of using OSB sheathing; removing a cast iron pipe obstructing structural beams and installing new post supports; repairing a historic window sash; removing the old wall of the ell.

title: This Old House
description:

Tom Silva adds insulation to the oldest part of the house; landscape designer Jenn Nawada and Roger build raised beds out of old fieldstone and Becky plants the first vegetables. Tom and Kevin waterproof the new roof with a self-sealing membrane.

title: This Old House
description:
S33 E08 — Bedford: Kitchen Inspiration
Replacing a rotted post; reinstalling the restored historic window sashes; upgrading the electrical service in the garage; the house that inspired the kitchen; removing strip flooring to reveal historic boards.

Honey harvesting; adding outlets.
